name: Mont de Conques – Pallars front strongholds
story: After the Nationalist Aragon offensive of spring 1938 the front in western Catalonia settled along the Segre and Noguera Pallaresa rivers. The Nationalists held bridgeheads at Tremp, Balaguer and Seròs. Mont de Conques, near Isona in the Conca de Tremp, was fortified by the Nationalists and attacked several times by the Republicans, especially in their May 1938 offensive against the Tremp and Balaguer bridgeheads, which failed at high cost. The line held until the Nationalist Catalonia offensive of December 1938. Republican positions such as the La Posa bunker at Abella de la Conca faced it across the valley.
see: Nationalist concrete positions and trenches on the hill; the Republican La Posa bunker at Abella de la Conca (42.13311, 1.07633) is nearby.
plan: Rough tracks from Conques (Camí Vell d'Isona); walking boots needed; no facilities.
